text:
erin: FYI customer reported a wire got rejected by beneficiary bank as 'invalid account number'. they attached the bank's return notice.

payments: Can you paste the original payload we sent? also what rail was used (SWIFT/correspondent)?

erin: customer says SWIFT MT103 out of our EU gateway. here's the sanitized payload they gave us:
```
{
  "amount": "12500.00",
  "currency": "USD",
  "beneficiary_name": "Acme Manufacturing",
  "beneficiary_account": "0012345678",  // leading zeros present in sender DOC
  "beneficiary_iban": "GB29 NWBK 6016 1331 9268 19",
  "bic": "NWBKGB2L"
}
```

alice: on our side the account number field is stored as a string, we don't strip zeros when creating the MT103. strange. :thinking:

payments: log from SWIFT gateway at time of send shows transformation step v2.3 did a numeric normalize on account numbers. looks like it removed leading zeros before formatting into the MT103 tag. snippet from gateway log:
```
INFO 2026-02-18T14:22:03Z transform.normalizeAccount -> input="0012345678" output="12345678"
```

ben: That would definitely cause the beneficiary bank to fail IBAN/account cross-check. many banks expect the BBAN portion to preserve leading zeros when constructing the IBAN. recipient's return text: 'INCOMPATIBLE_ACCOUNT_NUMBER: BBAN length mismatch'

customer: we require confirmation this is our formatting. our ERP outputs the leading zeros and we can't change that. we need the funds reissued asap and an explanation for accounting.

support-lead: apologies to the customer. payments, can we reissue quickly and avoid the transform? what's the blast radius if we revert normalize for legacy rails?

payments: quick plan: 1) mark the original transfer as returned; 2) create reissue transfer preserving beneficiary_account as-is and route via alternate correspondent (skip transform); 3) patch transform to only normalize for account fields known to be numeric-only (add whitelist). reissue ETA depends on compliance checks ~ 30-90 mins.

erin: customer asked for repro steps so their treasury team can confirm. payments — can you list exact steps we used so they can compare?

payments: repro steps (for internal / customer):
1) Call POST /v1/wires with payload (include beneficiary_account with leading zeros). Example payload we accepted:
```
POST /v1/wires
{
  "amount":12500.00,
  "currency":"USD",
  "beneficiary_account":"0012345678",
  "beneficiary_iban":"GB29NWBK60161331926819"
}
```
2) Our gateway transform service normalized the account field (bug) before generating MT103.
3) MT103 submitted, beneficiary bank validated BBAN vs IBAN, detected mismatch and initiated return.

ben: to validate locally you can generate the BBAN from the IBAN and compare to the account field; if they differ because of leading zeros it's reproducible.

customer: ok we'll run that check. can you also confirm if fees were charged and whether we'll refund any return fees?

support-lead: fees: the original send had our normal send fee (USD 25). return fees depend on correspondent bank — initial glance shows a USD 40 return charge on the intermediary. we should refund the send fee and absorb the return charge for this bug. finance signoff required.

alice: put a hold on further outgoing wires that use transform v2.3 and add a monitoring alert for account normalization mismatches. I'll push a hotfix to the gateway to preserve string account fields (PR coming).

payments-bot: incident created: PAY-2026-045. owners: @payments @eng-ml. SLA: customer update within 60m.

erin: thanks. I'll tell the customer we will reissue and refund send fees, ETA ~1h and will confirm when reissue is submitted. sending customer-facing blurb now.

customer: thanks for the quick triage. please include the returned MT103 and the new transaction id when reissued.

payments: noted — will attach returned MT103 and new ID in follow-up. follow-up actions:
- reissue preserving leading zeros, alternate correspondent
- refund send fee and cover return charge
- patch transform whitelist and add unit test to prevent regression
- postmortem if more than 2 customers impacted

erin: closing loop for now, tracking under PAY-2026-045. :white_check_mark:
